[ASSISTANT_SAID] The abstract is a brief summary of the paper, typically around 150-250 words, providing an overview of the research question, methods used, main findings, and conclusions drawn.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The introduction sets the stage for the paper, providing background information on the research topic and stating the research question or hypothesis, along with an overview of the methods used and the significance of the study.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The methods section should provide a detailed description of the research design, including sample size and population, data collection and analysis procedures, and any statistical tests used, written in enough detail for replication.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The results section presents the findings of the study, including statistical analyses and data visualizations, presented clearly and concisely with necessary explanations.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The discussion section interprets the results, relates them to broader literature, discusses study limitations, and implications for future research.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The conclusion summarizes the main findings and provides recommendations for future research.
